metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source with a deployable entry point (Dockerfile CMD node dist/server.js), a dependency manifest (package.json with Fastify/pg), and single-service IaC (infra/ecs.yaml). Single deployable service, not a monorepo or library.
metadata.archetype_justification: The service owns persistent state (PostgreSQL via pg.Pool in src/services/order-service.ts) and exposes create/delete/refund/cancel mutations alongside reads (src/routes.ts). It calls only one downstream collaborator (WarehouseClient), so it is not an orchestrator.
metadata.surface_flags_rationale: pg driver with a connection Pool and SQL against an orders table; Dockerfile plus infra/ecs.yaml ECS Fargate task/service; Fastify HTTP routes and openapi/orders.yaml; DesiredCount 2 on the ECS service; CloudFormation provisioning AWS::ECS::*, AWS::SecretsManager::Secret and AWS::IAM::Role - application-level only, which surface-gates SEC-Q1 out.

top_gaps.title: CI/CD Automation
top_gaps.gap: No pipeline definitions anywhere in the repo - no .github/workflows/, buildspec.yml, Jenkinsfile, or CodePipeline in IaC.
top_gaps.impact: Every image build, CloudFormation change, and migration is manual; blocks safe iteration on all other modernization work.

top_gaps.title: Encryption at Rest
top_gaps.gap: No KMS key, no encryption properties on any data surface; the RDS database the app uses is not defined in IaC at all.
top_gaps.impact: Order rows contain customer PII; no provable encryption-at-rest or key-rotation posture.

top_gaps.title: Integration Testing
top_gaps.gap: vitest is wired as the test script but the repo contains zero test files; no CI to run them.
top_gaps.impact: Refund and cancel paths with irreversible side effects have no automated regression safety net.

top_gaps.title: Backup and Recovery
top_gaps.gap: No backup retention, AWS Backup plan, PITR, or snapshot configuration; DELETE /orders/{id} hard-deletes rows.
top_gaps.impact: A hard delete or operator error is unrecoverable - no restore path exists in code or IaC.

top_gaps.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
top_gaps.gap: No SQS/SNS/EventBridge resources or SDK clients; refund and dispatch-recall cross a service boundary over a direct synchronous call.
top_gaps.impact: Tight synchronous coupling to the payment/warehouse collaborator; retries duplicate money movement.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: The application uses PostgreSQL through pg.Pool and README.md states 'PostgreSQL 15 on RDS', but infra/ecs.yaml contains no AWS::RDS::* resource - only the ECS cluster, task definition, service, execution role, and the orders/db secret. No MultiAZ, engine version, encryption, or backup configuration exists for the production database anywhere in the repo, so Multi-AZ failover cannot be demonstrated.
findings.gap: The production database is managed per documentation but has no in-repo definition, matching the Score 2 criterion 'managed but single-AZ / without Multi-AZ failover enabled'.
findings.recommendation: Declare the RDS/Aurora PostgreSQL instance in IaC with MultiAZ: true, a pinned EngineVersion, StorageEncrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, and BackupRetentionPeriod >= 7 days.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: OrderService.refund() and cancelAndRecallShipment() are multi-step business operations (database state transition followed by an external side effect) implemented as straight-line code with no state machine, retry policy, or compensating action. No Step Functions, Temporal, or workflow definition exists.
findings.gap: Business-critical multi-step operations are entirely hardcoded; if the external call fails after the database write the order is left in refunded/cancelled state with no recovery path.
findings.recommendation: Move the refund and cancel flows into AWS Step Functions with explicit retry, catch, and compensation states, or implement a transactional outbox so the external step can be retried idempotently.

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
findings.description: No managed messaging or streaming resources exist (no SQS/SNS/EventBridge/Kinesis/MSK in infra/ecs.yaml) and package.json declares no messaging SDK. Cross-boundary state changes (refund, dispatch recall) are direct synchronous calls on the injected WarehouseClient.
findings.gap: State changes cross a service boundary with no decoupling buffer; a timeout cannot be retried safely because there is no idempotency key, so the service is both tightly coupled and exposed to duplicate side effects.
findings.recommendation: Publish order state changes to EventBridge or SQS and have the payment/warehouse integration consume them with idempotent handlers and a DLQ, keeping the synchronous read path unchanged.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: The task runs in a customer-supplied VPC with awsvpc networking and AssignPublicIp: DISABLED, but no AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup is defined or attached, no subnet-tier distinction is enforced (SubnetIds is an untyped list), and there are no VPC endpoints, PrivateLink, or VPC Lattice resources.
findings.gap: Network segmentation is implicit and delegated to the parameter supplier; without an in-repo security group the task's ingress/egress posture is undefined and there is no least-privilege path to RDS, Secrets Manager, or ECR.
findings.recommendation: Define a task security group (ingress only from the ALB SG, egress restricted to the database SG and required endpoints), add VPC endpoints for Secrets Manager/ECR/CloudWatch Logs, and require private subnets explicitly.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: README.md describes an ALB, but infra/ecs.yaml contains no ElasticLoadBalancingV2, API Gateway, or CloudFront resource; the ECS service has no LoadBalancers block or target group. There is no in-repo managed entry point at all.
findings.gap: No throttling, request validation, WAF, or managed TLS termination is defined - and SAFETY.md explicitly flags the absence of rate limiting on mutating endpoints, which is a gateway-level control.
findings.recommendation: Add an internet-facing ALB in IaC (target group, health check, HTTPS listener, WAF association) or front the service with API Gateway using a JWT authorizer and usage-plan throttling.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: The ECS service is pinned at DesiredCount: 2 with no ApplicationAutoScaling ScalableTarget or ScalingPolicy. No database auto-scaling exists and no scheduled scaling is configured.
findings.gap: Capacity is entirely static - a traffic spike cannot be absorbed and off-peak capacity cannot be reclaimed.
findings.recommendation: Register the ECS service as a scalable target with target-tracking policies on CPU utilization and ALB RequestCountPerTarget, bounded by the database connection ceiling; add Aurora reader auto-scaling once the database is in IaC.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: No backup configuration of any kind was found: searched infra/ecs.yaml for AWS::Backup::*, BackupRetentionPeriod, PointInTimeRecoverySpecification, snapshot lifecycle, and S3 versioning - none present. Meanwhile OrderService.hardDelete() issues DELETE FROM orders with no soft-delete and no audit trail.
findings.gap: There is no demonstrable restore path for the only stateful component while the API exposes an unguarded hard delete of customer PII - an unrecoverable data-loss scenario.
findings.recommendation: Enable automated RDS backups with PITR and >= 7-day retention plus an AWS Backup plan with cross-region copy; convert hardDelete to a soft delete with an audit record; document and rehearse the restore procedure.

findings.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
findings.description: Compute is reasonably positioned (DesiredCount 2 on Fargate across a caller-supplied SubnetIds list, deployment circuit breaker with rollback), but the template does not constrain the number of AZs, there is no load balancer with cross-zone balancing, and the database has no Multi-AZ configuration in IaC.
findings.gap: The stateful tier's AZ posture is unenforced and fault isolation is not explicit.
findings.recommendation: Require at least two private subnets in distinct AZs, add an ALB with cross-zone load balancing, and set MultiAZ: true on the database when it is declared in IaC.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: A single CloudFormation template covers compute, the task execution role, logging, and the database secret. Not covered despite being depended on: the RDS database, the ALB described in README.md, security groups, auto-scaling, and all operational/DR resources (alarms, dashboards, backup plans).
findings.gap: Two surfaces this repo exposes - data and entry point/networking - have no in-repo IaC, and no operational resources are codified, so a meaningful fraction of the stack remains manual.
findings.recommendation: Extend the template (or add sibling templates) to cover RDS, ALB and target groups, security groups, Application Auto Scaling, and CloudWatch alarms/dashboards.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD definitions exist anywhere. Searched for .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml, appspec.yml, and CodePipeline/CodeBuild resources in infra/ecs.yaml - none found. package.json provides build, test, lint, and migrate scripts but nothing invokes them automatically, so image builds, CloudFormation changes, and node-pg-migrate schema migrations are all manual with no quality gates.
findings.gap: Both the application and IaC tracks are fully manual - there is no automation or gate between a commit and production.
findings.recommendation: Add a pipeline (GitHub Actions or CodePipeline/CodeBuild) with lint, build, test, scan, ECR push, CloudFormation change-set deploy, and ECS deployment stages, running migrations as an explicit gated stage.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication
findings.description: Every interaction is synchronous: inbound Fastify HTTP, outbound WarehouseClient.issueRefund and recallDispatch called inline in the request path. No message publishing, queue consumer, or event emission exists and package.json has no messaging SDK.
findings.gap: For a stateful-crud service, state changes other systems must act on propagate over synchronous calls only, and the caller holds the connection through a third-party money movement.
findings.recommendation: Emit domain events (order.refunded, order.cancelled) to EventBridge/SQS and move the payment and warehouse integrations to idempotent consumers, leaving reads and order creation synchronous.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: All five routes complete inline. POST /orders/{id}/refund and /cancel perform a database update then block on an external provider call of unbounded latency, returning 200 only when it finishes. There is no job framework, status endpoint, callback mechanism, or async invocation anywhere.
findings.gap: Operations whose duration depends on a third party run synchronously with no status-polling or callback path and, per SAFETY.md, no idempotency key - so a client timeout plus retry double-refunds.
findings.recommendation: Accept refund and cancel as 202 Accepted with a job id, process them asynchronously behind an Idempotency-Key, and expose a job-status endpoint for polling.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: openapi/orders.yaml declares info.version 2.1.0, but no endpoint is versioned: paths are /orders and /orders/{id}/..., the server URL has no version prefix, and src/routes.ts registers the same unversioned paths. No Accept-Version handling and no changelog exist.
findings.gap: Versioning is declarative metadata only - no runtime mechanism lets a consumer pin a version, so a breaking change hits all callers at once.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a single explicit scheme - prefix routes with /v1 via a Fastify plugin prefix and reflect it in the OpenAPI servers entry - and define a deprecation policy.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: External dependencies are addressed through environment variables with a hardcoded fallback (JWKS_URI defaults to https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json). No Cloud Map, service mesh, or registry resource exists and the ECS service has no ServiceRegistries block.
findings.gap: Endpoint resolution is configuration-based with no dynamic discovery, and the hardcoded JWKS fallback means a missing environment variable silently points at a default host.
findings.recommendation: Register the service in AWS Cloud Map and resolve collaborators via DNS-based discovery; remove the hardcoded JWKS fallback and fail fast when JWKS_URI/JWT_ISSUER are unset.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: The service handles only structured relational data - the Order interface is four scalar fields and all persistence is SQL against the orders table. No document, image, attachment, or export handling appears in src/, no S3/EFS/EBS resource exists in IaC, and no local-filesystem writing is performed.
findings.gap: There is no unstructured-data surface today, so no legacy-storage anti-pattern exists to remediate; equally there is no S3-backed object store or parsing pipeline should order documents be introduced.
findings.recommendation: No action required for the current surface. If order documents are introduced, store them in S3 with server-side encryption using a CMK and reference them by key from the orders table rather than storing blobs in PostgreSQL.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: All database access is centralized in a single class: OrderService receives one injected pg.Pool and every SQL statement in the codebase lives in its four methods. src/routes.ts and src/auth.ts contain no database imports.
findings.gap: SQL is embedded directly in the domain service rather than behind a dedicated repository abstraction - README.md describes a 'routes -> services -> repositories' layering, but the repository layer does not exist.
findings.recommendation: Extract an OrderRepository holding the SQL and have OrderService depend on it; this also makes the data layer substitutable for the integration tests missing per OPS-Q6.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: The engine version appears only in prose - README.md says 'PostgreSQL 15 on RDS'. infra/ecs.yaml declares no database resource and therefore no EngineVersion, and no compose or Helm values file pins a version. PostgreSQL 15 is a supported, non-EOL major version.
findings.gap: No version pinning exists in any deployment artifact, so the running engine version is implicit and EOL tracking is manual; no documented version-update procedure exists.
findings.recommendation: Pin EngineVersion explicitly when the database is declared in IaC, enable only minor-version auto-upgrade, and document the major-version upgrade procedure including rollback and downtime window.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: The system has a real data-at-rest surface (a PostgreSQL store holding customer PII, the orders/db secret, and the /ecs/orders log group) yet no encryption configuration exists: no AWS::KMS::Key, no KmsKeyId on the Secrets Manager secret, no StorageEncrypted (the database is not declared), and no KmsKeyId on the log group.
findings.gap: No customer-managed keys, no documented rotation, and no demonstrable encryption on the store holding order PII. AWS default encryption may apply at runtime but nothing in the repo asserts or enforces it.
findings.recommendation: Create a customer-managed KMS key for this service and reference it from the database (StorageEncrypted + KmsKeyId), the Secrets Manager secret, and the log group, with key rotation enabled and a key policy scoped to the task role.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: The service does not manage its own credentials - it delegates to an external identity provider, fetching signing keys from that provider's JWKS endpoint and validating JWT_ISSUER. There is no local user table, password hashing, or token issuance code anywhere in src/.
findings.gap: The IdP integration is token-validation only and configured by convention: no OIDC/SAML client registration, no SSO configuration, no Cognito/Okta/Ping resource in IaC, and a hardcoded JWKS fallback URL means the trust anchor is not pinned by deployment configuration.
findings.recommendation: Declare the identity integration explicitly (Cognito user pool or third-party OIDC client in IaC), require JWKS_URI and JWT_ISSUER with no fallback, and document the SSO flow and role-claim mapping.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: No plaintext credentials exist anywhere in the repository - no .env file, no password literals in source, no credentials in IaC. The database password is generated by AWS::SecretsManager::Secret (orders/db, GenerateSecretString) and delivered to the container through the task definition Secrets block as DB_PASSWORD.
findings.gap: No rotation is configured on the secret - there is no RotationSchedule or RotationLambdaARN - so the highest-risk credential is managed but static.
findings.recommendation: Attach AWS::SecretsManager::RotationSchedule with the managed RDS PostgreSQL rotation function once the database is declared in IaC, and verify the application reconnects on rotation.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: The image is reasonably constructed (multi-stage build, node:20-slim runtime, NODE_ENV=production, non-root USER node) and Fargate removes host patching. However there is no vulnerability scanning: no ECR ImageScanningConfiguration (no ECR repository is declared), no Inspector, no .snyk, and no dependency-update automation at any canonical Dependabot/Renovate path. The base image is an unpinned floating tag.
findings.gap: Nothing detects a vulnerable base image or transitive npm dependency and nothing drives routine patch uptake - the stack relies on manual rebuilds.
findings.recommendation: Declare an ECR repository with scan-on-push (or enable Inspector for ECR), pin the base image by digest and rebuild on a schedule, and add Dependabot or Renovate configuration for npm and Docker updates.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: There is no pipeline, therefore no security validation step. Searched for SAST configuration (SonarQube, Semgrep, CodeGuru), dependency scanning (npm audit in a pipeline, Dependabot/Renovate config), container scanning (ECR scan-on-push, Trivy), and .snyk policy files - none exist. package.json provides only lint, build, and test scripts, none automatically executed.
findings.gap: No SAST, no dependency scanning, no container scanning, and no blocking security gate before deployment.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI job running npm audit --audit-level=high, a SAST tool (Semgrep or CodeGuru Reviewer) over src/, and ECR image scanning, with the pipeline failing on critical findings.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No tracing instrumentation exists. package.json lists no OpenTelemetry, aws-xray-sdk, or ADOT dependency; infra/ecs.yaml has no X-Ray or ADOT sidecar and the task role has no X-Ray permissions. No traceparent or X-Amzn-Trace-Id handling appears in src/, including on outbound WarehouseClient calls.
findings.gap: Calls into the payment/warehouse collaborator and into PostgreSQL are untraceable end to end, so latency and failure attribution for the irreversible refund and cancel paths is guesswork.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation for Fastify and pg, export via an ADOT sidecar to X-Ray, and propagate trace context on outbound WarehouseClient calls.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: The surface gate is satisfied (has_api_surface and has_persistent_data_store are true). No monitoring artifacts exist in the repository: infra/ecs.yaml contains no CloudWatch alarm, dashboard, or latency/error-rate threshold, and there is no SLO file, error-budget definition, or availability target anywhere.
findings.gap: With zero in-repo monitoring artifacts there is not even an implicit SLO - the repository defines no acceptable latency or error rate for the order-management journeys.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for order read, order create, and refund with p99 latency and error-rate targets, express them as CloudWatch alarms in IaC, and track an error budget; if SLO tooling lives in an external platform, link those definitions from the repo.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics are emitted. There is no CloudWatch SDK dependency, no PutMetricData call or embedded-metric-format log line in src/, and no dashboard in IaC. Orders created, refunds issued and their amounts, and dispatch recalls are not counted anywhere.
findings.gap: Only default ECS/container infrastructure metrics are available, so refund volume and value, cancellation rate, and order throughput are invisible to operators - the signals needed to detect a runaway automated caller.
findings.recommendation: Publish counters and value metrics for order creation, refund count/amount, and cancellation via the CloudWatch embedded metric format from the existing structured logs, and build a service dashboard in IaC.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting is configured. infra/ecs.yaml declares no CloudWatch alarm, composite alarm, anomaly detector, SNS topic, or paging integration. Logs ship to /ecs/orders via the awslogs driver but no metric filter or alarm is attached.
findings.gap: Failures, latency regressions, and abnormal refund rates generate no signal - detection depends entirely on someone reading logs.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms for 5xx rate, p99 latency, and task restarts with an SNS notification target, plus anomaly detection on refund count and amount once business metrics exist.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy
findings.description: The surface gate is satisfied (has_deployed_workload is true). The ECS service uses the default rolling deployment with DeploymentCircuitBreaker enabled and Rollback true - meaningful protection - but there is no traffic shifting: no CodeDeploy resource, no appspec.yml, no weighted ALB target groups (no load balancer at all), and no feature flags. README.md's 'blue/green deploy on ECS' claim is unsupported by configuration.
findings.gap: Rolling deployment with health checks and rollback but no canary or blue/green traffic shifting - a regression that passes container health checks reaches 100% of traffic.
findings.recommendation: Adopt ECS blue/green via CodeDeploy (DeploymentController CODE_DEPLOY with an appspec.yml and two target groups) or canary traffic shifting on weighted ALB target groups, with CloudWatch alarms as the rollback trigger, and align README.md with the implementation.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: package.json declares 'test': 'vitest run' with vitest 1.4 as a dev dependency and README.md claims 'Unit + integration tests', but the repository contains no test files at all: a whole-tree search for *test*, *.spec.*, and test/ tests/ __tests__/ directories returned nothing. There is also no CI pipeline to execute tests.
findings.gap: No automated tests of any kind exist, so the irreversible hardDelete, refund, and cancelAndRecallShipment paths have zero regression coverage - and the documentation overstates the actual state.
findings.recommendation: Add integration tests for create -> read -> refund -> cancel against a containerized PostgreSQL with a stubbed WarehouseClient (the injected interface makes this straightforward) plus unit tests for requireRole, and wire vitest run into the pipeline as a blocking gate.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation
findings.description: The surface gate is satisfied (has_deployed_workload is true). No runbooks or remediation automation exist: no SSM Automation document, no Lambda remediation, no Step Functions incident workflow, no runbook files. SAFETY.md is a risk register with intended remediations, not an operational runbook - it has no detection steps, escalation path, or recovery procedure.
findings.gap: Incident response is entirely ad hoc, including for the two highest-consequence failure modes the repo itself documents (duplicate refund, erroneous hard delete).
findings.recommendation: Write structured runbooks for duplicate refund, erroneous delete, warehouse-recall failure, and database unavailability with detection, containment, and recovery steps; automate the mechanical ones as SSM Automation documents and add an alarm-triggered rollback path.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No ownership attribution for observability exists: no CODEOWNERS file, no dashboards or alarms to own (infra/ecs.yaml declares none), no SLO definition files, and no team or owner tag on any resource. The only operational configuration is the awslogs driver pointing at /ecs/orders.
findings.gap: Monitoring assets neither exist nor have named owners, so there is no accountable party for detection coverage.
findings.recommendation: Create a per-service CloudWatch dashboard and alarm set in IaC tagged with an owning team, add a CODEOWNERS entry covering infra/ and observability configuration, and record the on-call owner alongside the SLOs.

findings.title: Resource Tagging Governance
findings.description: The surface gate is satisfied - the repo provisions ECS, IAM, and Secrets Manager resources. No Tags property appears on any resource in infra/ecs.yaml: not the cluster, task definition, service, execution role, or secret. The only naming metadata is ClusterName: orders and the secret name orders/db. No tag policy or Config rule is referenced.
findings.gap: No cost-allocation, ownership, or environment tags exist, so spend cannot be attributed, ownership cannot be resolved during an incident, and environment cannot be distinguished from the resources themselves.
findings.recommendation: Add a consistent tag set (Service, Owner, Environment, CostCenter, DataClassification) to every resource or at the stack level so they propagate, activate the keys as cost-allocation tags, and enforce with an AWS Config required-tags rule.

evaluations.title: Managed Compute
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - all compute is ECS Fargate (AWS::ECS::Cluster/TaskDefinition with RequiresCompatibilities FARGATE/Service with LaunchType FARGATE); no EC2 instance, launch template, or ASG anywhere.

evaluations.title: Programming Languages
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - Node.js 20 with TypeScript 5.4 strict targeting ES2022, Fastify 4.26, jose 5; language, framework, and libraries are all current with first-class AWS SDK support.

evaluations.title: Monolith vs Microservices
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - single narrowly scoped service owning its own orders schema, clean acyclic layering (routes -> service -> pg), auth isolated, external collaborator behind an injected interface, one deployable unit.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - no .sql files and no CREATE PROCEDURE/TRIGGER/FUNCTION anywhere; all logic in TypeScript with parameterized standard SQL and application-layer migrations via node-pg-migrate.

evaluations.title: API Authentication
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - every route carries a requireRole preHandler; per-request RS256 JWT verification against a remote JWKS with issuer and audience enforcement and role-claim checks; OpenAPI declares global bearerAuth.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: Surface gate - the repo contains application-level IaC only (ECS cluster/task/service, task role, one service secret) with no account/foundation-level resources. CloudTrail is provisioned once per account or organization and belongs in the foundation infrastructure repo.

pathways.name: Move to Cloud Native
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: APP-Q2 < 3 AND at least one of INF-Q1 < 3, APP-Q3 < 3, APP-Q4 < 3

triggering_questions.note: APP-Q2 = 4 meets threshold; the service is already a single well-bounded unit owning its own data, so the primary trigger does not fire.

pathways.not_triggered_reason: Primary trigger (APP-Q2 < 3) not met; supporting conditions alone cannot trigger the pathway.

pathways.name: Move to Containers
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: INF-Q1 < 3 AND no container definitions found

triggering_questions.note: INF-Q1 = 4 meets threshold; a Dockerfile exists and the workload runs on ECS Fargate.

pathways.not_triggered_reason: Workload already runs on ECS Fargate with a container image; the contextual guard blocks this pathway.

pathways.name: Move to Open Source
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: DATA-Q4 < 3 AND commercial DB engines detected

triggering_questions.note: DATA-Q4 = 4 meets threshold; no stored procedures or proprietary SQL.

pathways.not_triggered_reason: No commercial database engine detected - the database is open-source PostgreSQL - and no proprietary SQL exists.

triggering_questions.note: Managed RDS asserted in README but absent from IaC; no Multi-AZ, encryption, or backup configuration for the production database.
Engine version documented in prose only, not pinned in any deployment artifact.

detail.current_state: PostgreSQL accessed via pg.Pool with the password injected from Secrets Manager by the ECS task definition, but infra/ecs.yaml declares no AWS::RDS::* resource - the database is unprovisioned, unversioned, unencrypted, unbacked-up and has no failover configuration in code.
migration_tools: AWS DMS (only if re-creating under IaC with minimal downtime)
immediate_actions: Declare the RDS/Aurora instance in IaC
Enable MultiAZ, StorageEncrypted with a CMK, and automated backups with PITR
Pin EngineVersion and document the upgrade/rollback procedure
Attach a rotation schedule to the orders/db secret

pathways.name: Move to Managed Analytics
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: INF-Q4 < 3 AND evidence of data processing workloads must exist

triggering_questions.note: Below threshold, but the contextual guard blocks the pathway.
Data access is centralized - no data source sprawl.

pathways.not_triggered_reason: Contextual guard: no streaming, ETL, Glue, Airflow, data lake, or analytics artifacts exist anywhere in the repo. This is a CRUD order API with no data-processing responsibility, so managed analytics is not a modernization gap here.

pathways.name: Move to AI
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: No AI/agent frameworks, vector DB, RAG, or eval framework - requires AI/agent/LLM intent evidenced in the repository
pathways.not_triggered_reason: No AI/agent intent evidenced in the repository (no AI-related signal terms in dependencies, source, configuration, IaC, or documentation). A case-insensitive scan for agentic, LLM, machine learning, Bedrock, generative AI, GenAI, RAG, vector database/store, embedding, copilot, chatbot, AI agent, AI-powered, and large language model returned no matches.
